comparator.academicYear: Adopted OER 2026–27 for students starting in 2026; checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER establishes a 120-EC major and 60-EC profiling space. The major comprises eight compulsory 7.5-EC foundation courses (60 EC), Schrijven, redeneren & presenteren and Informatiekunde (15 EC), one compulsory-choice 30-EC deepening package, CIW-Lab (7.5 EC) and the BA-eindwerkstuk (7.5 EC). Four formal deepening packages are listed. Because the normalized target names no package, the first-listed package, Media, data en maatschappij, is selected independently of UCR fit under the official-order tiebreak. The 60-EC profiling space remains open, including the requirement for a coherent 30-EC profiling package.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The target names the ordinary CIW bachelor but no deepening package. The adopted OER lists four equal-status compulsory-choice packages and places Media, data en maatschappij first. It is therefore selected neutrally from official order, not because of similarity to UCR; the 60-EC profiling space remains genuinely open.

Two further formal packages support coherent, substantially distinct UCR alternatives in media markets and organisational interaction. The fourth formal package, culture and diversity, remains academically defensible but is excluded by the maximum of three alternatives; its subject matter is still represented across included courses.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce frameworks for analysing communication and its effects.
Both examine how formal choices in messages produce meaning; UCR concentrates on linguistic style.
Both analyse communication in interaction; UCR approaches it through applied rhetoric.
Both examine influence and the design of more effective messages.
Both connect language and communication to cognitive or technological systems, while the comparator gives greater emphasis to generative AI and societal implications.
The comparator's dedicated academic writing, reasoning and presentation course has no sufficiently direct single UCR counterpart.
Both introduce media institutions, forms and their relationship with society.
Both examine how media technologies develop and reshape communication, though UCR is more historically oriented.
Both study platform-era media production, creators and audience participation.
The integrated comparator component combines mediatisation, datafication, social platforms and critical issues; no unused single UCR course adequately represents that full primary focus.
Both develop empirical research design, data collection, analysis and interpretation; UCR emphasises qualitative methodology.
Both prepare students to design and execute advanced research; the comparator lab directly develops the thesis proposal.
Both analyse visual information and how formal image features shape interpretation, with UCR using computational image methods.
Both develop foundational understanding of information and its organisation; UCR is more data-analytic.
Both use computational methods and AI critically in research; the comparator focuses on digital media and society.
The comparator requires a 7.5-EC independent research project; UCR's standardized optional independent research element is displayed alongside it.
The comparator's 60-EC profiling space remains open, including its coherent 30-EC package requirement.

notes.text: Utrecht CIW combines a prescribed communication core, one coherent 30-EC deepening package, a dedicated CIW research lab and compulsory bachelor thesis with 60 EC of profiling space. UCR can build strong media-data, media-market and organisational-communication programmes, but it does not reproduce each Utrecht package course-for-course or require an equivalent CIW thesis; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
